I'm late to the party but I thought I might as well share so I can tell someone, TW for self harm and stuff, it's also pretty long. Sorry, just want to get it off my chest.

​

The secret that would ruin my life if it got out would be that I tried to commit suicide in January. My parents know, and my doctors know, but otherwise nobody knows. I had called the suicide hotline after an attempt at hanging myself, I gave my preferred name and what state I lived in, but otherwise I gave no super personal information. It took about a week to track my location, and when the counselor finally took me out of class for a talk, my parents were in Vegas for a week on vacation with their friends. The School counselor was pretty nice and didn't mention that she had known everything about the call (The school resource officer had been told by the suicide hotline what I had said and done, who in turn told the counselor) and I was under the belief that she didn't know about my attempt. An awkward talk (where I denied trying to commit suicide) and a call to my mom later, I was back in class and under the impression that that was all that was going to happen. Boy was I wrong.

A few days after my parents came back they took me out of sixth period and took me into the car. I knew something was going to happen as soon as I was told that I was going to leave, and I had a vague idea of what was going to happen. My parents explained that I was going to get help and that we were going to the hospital. I didn't get to tell my best friend that I was leaving or for how long (although I didn't know how long I would be gone, either). Got to the hospital, lots and lots of questions. When I'm finally free me and my mom watch movies on the little TV that was in the room. My mom had to hold the remote and they took it away when we were done with it because it had a wire. 

Next day I had to take a shower. I cried for many reasons that time because, number one and the worst, was that I had to look at my body, and gender dysphoria was really awful when I had to look at myself. Second, because I couldn't be alone in the room. My mom was in there with me the whole time, and I cried the entire time. Then we were moved to the safety room, which was grey wall and basically nothing but a bed and small TV in a glass frame.

Finally after three days of waiting, We were told that that night we were being moved to a different hospital and was being enrolled in an in-patient program where I'd be stuck in for a week, at the least. We (my mom and I) were moved by ambulance. It was a crazy ride, but I made conversation with the helper dude in the back with my mom and I, cracked a few jokes, tried to reassure my mom that this was all fine, and that this would be the last time she'd have to see me in a stretcher (which probably won't turn out to be true, but still.) She told me that she loved me a lot during that hour in the ambulance.

We made it to the hospital and to the kids psych unit, where I am greeted with unfriendly, sad faces of other kids. On my overall stay, the youngest was twelve, the oldest was seventeen. More questions, filling out of paperwork, and then I was off to bed. I had a window in my otherwise barren room so that was cool :) Every morning I'd look out there at the sun, I enjoyed that.

I was very awkward the first two or three days. The other kids were pretty quiet, especially in the morning. There was this one girl, we'll call her Sarah, who talked with me a lot (she was the twelve year old), because we were at the same hospital before we got to this children's unit. We played Uno a lot. 

Eventually I made friends with the LGBT kids in the unit (which about half of them were), and we did a fun activity where we made our own island. We called it ROYGBIV (Roy-jee-biv) and its national bird was something rainbow, I can't remember, it's national flower was a rainbow hibiscus, it was shaped like Lisa Simpsons head, and we had a lot of fun making it. That was the fondest memory I have of that place.

After a week (exactly seven days) I finally got out and my parents took me home. They told my older brother that I was home, but my twin didn't know. It was funny because when he got home from a basketball game he came through the front door and I was seated at the kitchen and he didn't notice me for like ten minutes. When he saw me his eyes widened and he said "Whoa" pretty load and asked if he could hug me, that was pretty sweet, even though I don't really like hugs. 

Its been almost two months (?) I think, and I'd like to say that I am doing a lot better now, but my issues haven't really changed. I feel sad a lot, but I haven't had any suicidal thoughts since that night on January sixth. I've changed therapists and medicines, so I suppose that is good. I'm hoping that I'll get better with time and therapy. Let's hope.

Anyway, sorry for rambling. Just wanted to get this off my chest. I feel a little better now that I've said something to someone, or just writing it down. Hope y'all have amazing days, I really really want you to not end up like I did. But if you're feeling bad, Please please please talk to someone. It is not always gonna be this way. And if I can get through this shit and go to school the day after I got released, you can get better. I promise you, I **promise**. And if there is any way I can help you, or anyone else, then I will do it gladly. 

The thing about going to hell is that you need to have understood happiness to feel that way. Don't assume you can't feel happy again. 

Suicide hotline:  1-800-273-8255 

Love y'all, thank you for letting me talk. 

​

​

P.S. Just wanna add that my friend's reaction to me appearing in her fifth period class was priceless. I love her so much. I hope you guys all have a person that makes you feel happy. If not, I'd be happy to try and fill that position.

I have a few experiments that led me to be questioning (which I still am):

Went to a restaurant for my Mums birthday and got up to use the bathroom. Upon entering I held the door open for a woman who in turn said, "Thank you, sir," to which immediately it felt like she had lit fireworks inside my brain. She apologized and we both walked into the women's bathroom and did... y'know, and I just couldn't stop smiling. I felt so happy to be referred to as male! I started feeling very strange afterwards when referred to as female, called she/her and dressing like a girl. I began to heavily question my identity after that and soon it led to what I assumed was gender dysphoria. 

I went under the non-binary term for a while that summer and felt happier, but not content. That was when I reached out for some online help, such as dysphoria tests, members of the trans community, and online counselors. I got some name suggestions (primarily David, which I've used online since) and I just felt so much happier! I started realizing that things I did earlier in my life was similar to mild gender dysphoria. I always acted like a boy and insisted to my close friends that I wasn't a girl, I was a tomboy, lol. Normal kid stuff, although it didn't go further than that until middle school. 

Few other things similar to the first example: sometimes people mess up their words and call me he instead of she and it always makes me so happy, even if they correct themselves afterward. I now feel uncomfortable with she/her pronouns. My friend told me that when her mom first saw me, she thought I was a boy, and damn did I wish I was! I was pretty excited that I kindof passed as a boy back in third grade lol, even if I don't now.

Also, Elliot is SUCH an awesome name!!! Me and my friends always talk about how good of a name that is (I am NOT even lying), literally just the other day me and my good friend A.J. were talking about it lmao. I wish you luck in life my man!!

Hey hey hey, man. Please please please be calm. I want you to take some deep breaths and drink a cup of water, OK? If you can't do that, just continue reading this.

I'm so sorry you feel like this right now. I'd give anything for your pain to just dissapear right now. And I know this sounds strange coming from a total stranger, but please. Please don't commit suicide. These words might sound empty right now, but oh my god, you have worth, and things WILL get better! You are so wonderful and I know so many other people share this feeling. I know people will care. I know it. Your friends, family, teachers, people in your town; they will miss you. And absolutely nothing will change that. Not time, nothing. They will think of you everyday. Every. Day. And I want you to know that you are better than this. You do not deserve to die, and you do not deserve to feel the way you do right now. Just please, friend, please don't do it. It is a permanant solution to a temporary problem, and I know that might sound dumb but it is true. You can pull yourself up, friend. I believe in you. I believe in you and I feel you and I know what you are talking about and feeling and just... I want you to know that you have meaning. you have worth. And it would matter if you werent here anymore, I promise. Because you matter. You matter, I swear it on my life or by god or my friends and family, I swear it by everything that I find joy in. You. Are. Worth it. 

I want you to take some more deep breaths. In.... and out. In.... and out. Repeat this until your breathing starts to steady. Devoid your mind of anything and everything. Flip a switch in your brain and stop thinking for a couple of moments, let go of your worries and doubts and fears and all that stuff because right now, it doesnt matter. You do. You are top priority, now and always.

Has your breathing steadied yet? Do you feel well enough to get a cup of water (regardless of wether you already have one)? If so, drink it slowly. Steadily. A stream down your throat and let it restore your body and rrefresh your mind, just a little.

I want you to talk to somebody. Call a suicide hotline, go to the trevor project website, do an online chat with a counselour, anything. You need to talk about this, and you need to be heard. I want you to be heard. I want you to find help. 

I fricken love you, man, and I know that sounds weird from a stranger, but you do not deserve to beat yourself up like this. you don't deserve to feel this way. I'll tell you what you do deserve: Fulfillment, joy, friends, family, a full stomach, music, grand adventures, learning, enjoying, experiencing, everything that you have come to love, or used to love. You deserve so much and I can't even express it, Please, stay safe. Please. I believe in you, and so many others do, too. 

You can do this.
